=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:29-30 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The test expects `reason=marker_missing` when restore runs without a marker, but the helper exits silently.
  WHY: The assertion fails because the helper produces empty stderr on this path.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 56 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits silently when the marker is missing instead of emitting the expected `reason=marker_missing` diagnostic.
  WHY: The isolation test expects that diagnostic; the script exits with empty stderr, so the test fails.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 78-92 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any `https://github.com/` origin without verifying that its repository matches the trusted workflow repository.
  WHY: An editor can change origin to an attacker-controlled GitHub repository, and restore then injects `GH_TOKEN` into that destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-93 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts untrusted extraheader scopes and restores generic extraheaders without scoping them to the verified repository.
  WHY: The token can be sent to other GitHub repositories, and the tests expecting an origin-scoped key and rejection of attacker-scoped keys fail.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 19-54 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not detect or reject pre-existing credentialed push URLs or `pushInsteadOf` routing rules.
  WHY: Those credentials or alternate push destinations remain available to the editor after hide.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 55-101 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Restore does not validate `pushurl` or `pushInsteadOf` routing before injecting `GH_TOKEN`.
  WHY: An editor-changed push route can direct the restored token to an attacker-controlled destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 61-97 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into each checkout before validating all checkout entries.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, an earlier checkout already contains the token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 21-28 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide exits successfully when a stale marker exists or marker creation fails.
  WHY: The caller can proceed to launch the editor while checkout credentials remain visible.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 19-54 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate that `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is present and identifies the trusted checkout.
  WHY: The helper cannot establish the trusted repository identity needed to protect credential handling.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 57-60 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully when `GH_TOKEN` is missing.
  WHY: Callers cannot detect failed credential restoration and subsequent workflow Git operations may run unauthenticated; OpenAI rated this major rather than blocker.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 98-102 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits with status 0 even when validation or configuration failures set `failed=true`.
  WHY: Workflow callers cannot detect restoration failures; OpenAI rated this major rather than blocker.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py: lines 660-663 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_diagnostic_text` is defined but has no callers.
  WHY: The diagnostics path uses `_diagnostic_fingerprint` instead, leaving this helper as dead code.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 96 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `failed` variable is not reset between loop iterations, so later successful entries can log `outcome=warn`.
  WHY: The restore diagnostics become misleading after an earlier item fails.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 19-102 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The helper does not enforce the documented credential-isolation trust boundary.
  WHY: The combined gaps in repository validation, push routing, extraheader scoping, and failure status allow the workflow to inject credentials into untrusted destinations and prevent callers from detecting failures.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The credential helper rejects failed hides/restores and restores auth only when the origin still names the workflow's original repository (or its trusted support checkout) and its push URL agrees, not an editor-changed GitHub destination; generic GitHub extraheaders are restored scoped to the verified origin only."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh accepts any `https://github.com/` origin, does not validate repository identity or push routing, restores extraheaders without verified repository scoping, does not validate all checkouts before token injection, returns success on hide/restore failures, and does not emit the missing-marker diagnostic.
- requirement: "Their editor processes drop GitHub/Telegram credentials and the raw-evidence directory pointer, and temporarily hide git checkout credentials; network access for the model remains available."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh lacks the described credential-boundary hardening, including `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` checks, push-routing validation, all-checkout pre-validation, scoped extraheader restoration, and non-zero failure exits.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py: 29-30 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF added an assertion that `restore` called without a prior `hide` emits `reason=marker_missing` in stderr. The script `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh` line 56 executes `[ -s "${marker}" ] || exit 0`, which exits silently with return code 0 and empty stderr. The `"reason=marker_missing" in ""` check evaluates to False.
  WHY: Every run of `tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py` in CI will fail on this assertion. The editor summary from the prior run (entry[11]) claimed to have edited the script to emit this diagnostic, but the merge commit `[ai-merge-resolve]` (705f956) only carried pr_merge_status_guard.py changes and lost the script edit while keeping the test change.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 81-84 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: During credential restoration, the origin URL is validated only by checking if it starts with https://github.com/, without verifying the repository owner and name against the trusted repository identity (GITHUB_REPOSITORY or the trusted support repository).
  WHY: An untrusted or prompt-injected editor process running in the danger-full-access sandbox can change the git origin URL to point to an attacker-controlled repository on github.com (e.g., https://github.com/attacker/repo.git). Upon restore, editor_git_credentials.sh accepts the URL because it matches ^https://github\.com/, injects the privileged GH_TOKEN into remote.origin.url, and subsequent git fetch or push commands in the workflow transmit the token to the attacker repository. In addition, tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:53-68 (test_restore_does_not_send_token_to_an_editor_changed_origin) expects restore to fail and reject token injection, but the test fails.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-93 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Extraheader restoration accepts any extraheader matching ^http\.https://github\.com/[^[:space:]]*\.extraheader$ without verifying that the repository path in the key matches the checkout repository, and restores generic unscoped extraheaders without rewriting them to be repository-scoped.
  WHY: An editor can inject an extraheader key scoped to an attacker-controlled repository, causing restore to write the bearer token header for that destination. Additionally, restoring generic unscoped extraheaders (http.https://github.com/.extraheader) causes git to send GH_TOKEN on all requests directed to github.com. This causes tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:156-166 (test_restore_rejects_untrusted_extraheader_scope) to fail, and causes test_git_credentials_hidden_and_restored_without_marker_secrets (lines 42-43) to fail with CalledProcessError when looking for the repository-scoped key http.https://github.com/owner/repo.git.extraheader.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 19-54 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The hide and restore actions do not validate or handle remote.origin.pushurl or url.<base>.pushInsteadOf configurations.
  WHY: If an explicit credentialed pushurl or a pushInsteadOf rewrite exists prior to editor execution, hide ignores it and leaves credentials exposed in git configuration during editor execution. If an editor configures pushurl or pushInsteadOf during its run to point to an attacker repository, restore does not detect or reject the altered push routing. This breaks tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py test cases test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url, test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch, test_hide_rejects_preexisting_push_url_rewrite, and test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url_rewrite.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 61-97 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The restore loop inspects checkouts and injects credentials sequentially in a single pass without validating all checkouts before mutating any of them.
  WHY: In a multi-checkout environment (GITHUB_WORKSPACE and .codex-workflow-src), if the primary repository passes validation but the secondary checkout has been tampered with or points to an untrusted origin, the primary repository has already had GH_TOKEN injected before the secondary checkout fails. This causes tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:181-196 (test_restore_validates_every_checkout_before_injecting_any_token) to fail because the primary repository configuration already contains the secret.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 57-60 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When GH_TOKEN is unset or empty during restore, the script logs a warning and exits with status 0 instead of failing closed.
  WHY: If GH_TOKEN is missing, checkout credentials cannot be restored, leaving subsequent workflow git steps unauthenticated or in an unexpected state. In tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:48-49, assert missing.returnc
